subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: The 2012 Facebook IPO Glitch
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The 2012 Facebook IPO Glitch.

hook.text: Facebook's IPO was the most anticipated in years. NASDAQ's system choked and delayed trading for 30 minutes.

buildup.text: NASDAQ's order-matching engine received an unprecedented flood of orders in the opening minutes.

discovery.text: A race condition in the system's opening cross calculation failed to establish the right starting price.

twist.text: Traders couldn't confirm their orders for hours. Some unknowingly bought shares they didn't want.

climax.text: NASDAQ paid $62 million in penalties. The glitch shook confidence in electronic trading infrastructure.

punchline.text: The biggest IPO, broken by a race condition. Testing missed it.

quiz.question: What caused the NASDAQ Facebook IPO glitch?
options: A race condition in the order-matching engine
